newsitem.title: JAPAN: Kampo says investments yielded Y200 bln forex profit.
newsitem.headline: Kampo says investments yielded Y200 bln forex profit.

text.p: Japan's Postal Life Insurance System (Kampo) said on Tuesday its foreign bond investments had yielded forex profits of about 200 billion yen at the end of the last fiscal year.
The 1996/97 fiscal year ended on March 31.
The calculations were based on the end-March dollar/yen rate of 124.10 yen.
Kampo had a forex loss of 223.9 billion yen a year earlier.
Of Kampo's outstanding assets of 98,796.9 billion yen as of the end of fiscal 1996/97, foreign bond investment totalled 4,394.8 billion yen, up 17.7 percent from a year earlier.
Its investment in U.S. government and corporate bonds accounted for 31.2 percent of the total foreign bonds held by Kampo, a Kampo official said.

Kampo increased its investment in JGBs, government-guaranteed bonds and domestic municipal bonds in fiscal 1996/97, seeking investments with both high liquidity and creditworthiness, the official said.

Kampo's outstanding holdings of JGBs and government-guaranteed bonds stood at 36,151.8 billion yen in the last fiscal year, up 17.4 percent from a year earlier, and accounted for 36.6 percent, or the largest share, of its assets.
The value of municipal bond holdings totalled 6,407.0 billion yen, up 29.4 percent from the year earlier period.
Kampo also increased its bank deposits in 1996/97 as a short-term investment tool, the official said.
The value of its bank deposits totalled 5,575.3 billion yen, up 33.6 percent from a year earlier.
Kampo's total assets rose only 6.9 percent in 1996/97 from a year earlier, the lowest growth since 1964/65.
